_comment: Template every vSECC board's OCPP 1.6J config is generated from. Do not edit the generated files -
edit this, then re-run the generator in the EVerest-MCP repo:
python3 sim/make_vsecc_ocpp_configs.py --prefix YOURNAME_EVEREST            (dry run)
python3 sim/make_vsecc_ocpp_configs.py --prefix YOURNAME_EVEREST --live     (real CSMS)
See the CSMS section of .devcontainer/README.md.
Three fields differ per board and are set by the generator - everything else is identical:
Internal.ChargePointId        set by sim/make_vsecc_ocpp_configs.py --prefix, per board
Internal.ChargeBoxSerialNumber  a BASE, not a per-board value - the generator appends -1, -2, -3
Security.AuthorizationKey     the key the CSMS issued for THAT charge point. Never commit it.
NumberOfConnectors is 2 because one vSECC serves two connectors. Connector ids restart at 1 on
each board, so all three boards report connectors 1 and 2 - EVerest forces that.
DisableSecurityEventNotifications is true because libocpp carries SecurityEventNotification.req in
the TRANSACTION queue, which is strictly ordered with one message in flight. A CSMS that does not
answer one - Monta does not - leaves it stuck at the head, and every StartTransaction, MeterValues
and StopTransaction behind it is stranded. The symptom is brutal: the charger charges perfectly,
connection_status still reads connected, and the CSMS never learns the transaction exists, so its
own stop button fails with no message on the wire at all. Observed 2026-08-11 with 41 messages
stranded behind 18 boot notices. The flag also drops already-persisted ones at startup, so setting
it clears an existing jam.
AuthorizationCacheEnabled is false deliberately, and this is a test-rig decision rather than a
faithful one. libocpp caches every idTagInfo the CSMS returns and, per OCPP 1.6, honours a cached
Blocked without asking again - LocalPreAuthorize false does not change that. On a real charger that
is what carries it through a CSMS outage. On this rig it means a token you have just fixed in the
CSMS keeps being refused locally, with no message on the wire to say why, until someone deletes the
row from AUTH_CACHE. That cost an afternoon on 2026-08-11. Turn it back on if the cache itself is
what is being tested.
CompositeScheduleDefaultLimitWatts is what the CSMS assumes when no profile is active. It is set
to 375 kW to match what a Voltempo connector can actually deliver. Monta's own default is 240 kW,
which would silently cap every session a third below the cable rating and make the charger's 80 kW
power-sharing steps invisible above five vehicles. A charging profile is only observable if it
asks for less than this figure.
